messages:
alex-infra: Heads-up: were planning the Cloud KMS pattern for the next private deployment. Question: whats the recommended layout for keyrings/service accounts if the customer wants keys in their project but we need to do envelope encryption and occasional rewraps?

devon-sec: Short answer: prefer customer-owned keyring + a minimal impersonation-only svcacct in customer project. Keeps audit and control with customer, but lets our runtime rewrap.

maria-ops: Agree. Practical pattern Ive used:
- Customer creates project `proj-cust-<id>` and keyring `redwood-private-kr`
- They create a service account `redwood-kms-agent@proj-cust-<id>.iam.gserviceaccount.com` and grant it only the KMS roles it needs
- Our runtime uses short-lived tokens via Workload Identity Pool to impersonate that SA for encrypt/decrypt/rewrap ops

charlie-sre: Key IAM bindings we apply (customer side):
```
gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding proj-cust-<id> \
  --member="serviceAccount:redwood-kms-agent@proj-cust-<id>.iam.gserviceaccount.com" \
  --role="roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator"

# KMS bindings on the key itself
gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding redwood-private-kr --location=global --key=enc-key \
  --member="serviceAccount:redwood-kms-agent@proj-cust-<id>.iam.gserviceaccount.com" \
  --role="roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter"
```
This avoids giving broad project roles to our infra.

devon-sec: Important notes:
- Use IAM condition to limit `serviceAccountTokenCreator` to callers from our workload identity pool (restrict by `request.auth.claims[aud]` or `attribute.actor`), so tokens only issued when coming from our Dedicated/private runtime.
- Audit logs: enable `DATA_ACCESS` and `ADMIN_READ` for KMS in customer's project so key usage appears in their audit logs. Also export logs to their Logging sink if they want SIEM ingestion.

alex-infra: For envelope encryption flow: our runtime keeps a per-deployment envelope key (DEK) encrypted with the customer's KMS (KEK). We store the wrapped DEKs in our metadata store. Does that match what youre recommending?

maria-ops: Yes. Pattern: DEK is a symmetric key (generated by runtime), use KMS `encrypt` to wrap it. On decrypt path: `decrypt` -> use DEK to decrypt payload. Rewrap strategy: when rotating KMS key/version, call `gcloud kms keys versions create` to create new version then re-encrypt all DEKs by calling `encrypt` with new key and update wrapped DEKs atomically.

charlie-sre: Example rewrap pseudo: 
```
# create new key version
gcloud kms keys versions create enc-key --keyring=redwood-private-kr --location=global --project=proj-cust-<id>
# get new key version resource name
NEW=projects/proj-cust-<id>/locations/global/keyRings/redwood-private-kr/cryptoKeys/enc-key/cryptoKeyVersions/2
# runtime: for each wrapped_dek -> unwrap with old key, encrypt with NEW, update DB.
```
Make sure this runs in a migration job with idempotency and backoff, and keep old key version enabled until all DEKs rewrapped.

devon-sec: Also consider offline compromise scenarios: if customer insists on key material never leaving their HSM (CMEK/HSM), we can integrate with external HSM-backed KMS; the same envelope flow still works but rewraps are initiated by customer or by our agent when allowed.

alex-infra: How do we handle short-lived permissions and least privilege in practice?

maria-ops: Two levers: 1) Workload Identity Federation + impersonation so we never hold long-lived SA keys; 2) IAM conditions + narrow roles (cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter only, plus tokenCreator). If you need to list keys, add `cloudkms.viewer` at resource-level not project-level.

charlie-sre: One operational gotcha: `encrypt`/`decrypt` show up in Data Access logs which are disabled by default in many orgs. Make sure customer turns them on or we wont see KMS usage in audit. Also add a log-based metric for `methodName:\"Encrypt\" OR methodName:\"Decrypt\"` to alert on spikes.

devon-sec: For emergency key rotation / compromise: have a runbook:
1) disable compromised key version
2) create new key version
3) run rewrap job to move wrapped DEKs to new KEK
4) rotate service account keys/impersonation if SA was compromised
5) notify customer and update audit record

sre-bot: Incident template created: https://infra.redwood.internal/kw/incident-templates/kms-rewrap-runbook (generated) :white_check_mark:

alex-infra: This is great. Last Q: do we ever recommend giving our runtime `roles/cloudkms.admin`?

devon-sec: No. We should avoid admin. Minimal set: `roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter` on the key, and `roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator` on the SA (with condition). Anything else is overprivileged.

maria-ops: I'll draft a short onboarding checklist for customers (keyring + SA creation, IAM bindings, log exports, rotation cadence). Will post in #eng-security once done. :thumbsup:
